data.signal_type: Junior and mid-tier miners awarded DMRE mining rights without on-site processing infrastructure
data.description: New mining rights granted in Mpumalanga often go to junior miners and BEE mining companies who do not have capital to build dedicated washing plants. These operations produce ROM coal that requires third-party toll washing before it can meet export or even Eskom quality specifications.

data.signal_type: Washery shutdowns, maintenance outages, or closures at integrated mine plants
data.description: When a major integrated mine-washery goes offline for planned or unplanned maintenance, the displaced ROM coal requires diversion to third-party toll washing facilities. Optimum Coal's complex history and illegal mining activity at its wash plant signals recurring operational instability in the Woestalleen corridor.

data.signal_type: Tightening export quality specifications (API4/RB1 compliance pressure)
data.description: Export buyers and shipping counterparties increasingly enforce strict quality gates. ROM coal with ash content above 20â€“25% ADB cannot be sold into RB1 or RB2 markets without DMS processing. As the thermal coal export market tightens quality requirements, more ROM coal requires beneficiation before it can be placed with export buyers.

data.signal_type: Artisanal and small-scale miners (ASMs) and informal operators lacking processing access
data.description: The 2025 parliamentary oversight visit to Mpumalanga noted widespread illegal mining activity and illegal use of wash plant infrastructure (including Optimum Coal). This signals an unmet demand for accessible, legally compliant toll washing services for small-scale operators. Veralogix Plant is positioned to capture the compliant segment of this demand.
